name: Stratum MagLine Transit Operator Day Rig
description: A sharp, company-issued uniform built for transit operators running M88's elevated rail and underground tube lines. The core is a structured navy polyblend jacket with Stratum Logistics' orange-and-grey chevron shoulder patch stitched directly into the seam — not ironed on, not going anywhere. The jacket has a mandarin collar, snap-close breast pockets, and a left-chest embroidered name panel in block lettering. Underneath sits a moisture-wicking charcoal thermal base layer with a half-zip neck, designed to regulate body temperature through platform heat surges and cold tunnel drafts. Trousers are navy cargo-cut with reinforced knees, two side cargo pockets sealed with magnetic closures, and a low-profile tool loop on the right thigh for fare scanner holsters or comms clips. A hi-vis orange stripe runs the outer leg seam — retro-reflective in low light. Boots are the Veldtmann Steelcap 7 equivalent construction: thick rubber composite sole, steel toe cap, ankle support wrap, and oil-resistant tread. A charcoal knit watch cap with a small Stratum emblem on the cuff finishes the head. The whole kit reads institutional but maintained — pressed enough to mean the wearer takes the job seriously, worn enough to mean they've been doing it for years.
functionality: Thermal regulation for hot platform and cold tunnel environments, cargo pockets for fare equipment and tools, retro-reflective leg stripe for rail-adjacent visibility, magnetic pocket closures prevent tool loss, steel-toe boot construction, name panel for passenger-facing identification.
what_it_says: This is a person with a steady job and a union card. The Stratum patch means benefits, a pension if they live long enough, and a supervisor somewhere filing their hours. The wear on the jacket elbows says they've been at it long enough to stop caring what the fresh recruits think. Reliable. Present. Not going anywhere.
manufacturer: Stratum Logistics (corponation-issued uniform contract, manufactured by Kessler Fabricworks subsidiary)
price_range: Φ180–Φ240 (company-subsidized; out-of-pocket replacement cost after damage deduction)
story_hooks: A transit operator's name patch reads a name the player recognizes — someone reported missing three weeks ago. The uniform is being worn by someone else entirely.

The retro-reflective leg stripe has been partially scraped off on one operator's uniform — deliberately, not from wear — suggesting they've been moving through sections of tunnel they don't want to be seen in.

Stratum just changed their uniform contract supplier. The new jackets have a slightly different emblem. Someone in the old uniform is still running a route that was officially discontinued six months ago.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sharp, utilitarian uniform silhouette projecting institutional authority and working-class competence. The structured navy jacket with mandarin collar creates a compact, professional torso line. The hi-vis orange leg stripe and cap create bright accent points against the navy base. On a body, reads as someone who has earned their place in the transit infrastructure—clean but lived-in.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not restrictive; jacket sits close through the shoulders with room for movement through the torso. Cargo trousers have a straight cut from hip to ankle with reinforced articulation points at the knees. Boots provide ankle stability with a grounded, wide stance. Overall fit suggests functionality over fashion—built for 12-hour shifts moving between platform and cabin.
physical_description.primary_material: Navy polyblend synthetic jacket (wrinkle-resistant, stain-treated); charcoal moisture-wicking thermal base layer (synthetic blend with thermal regulation); cargo trousers in heavy-duty navy twill composite; Veldtmann composite boots with rubber and synthetic leather construction.
physical_description.texture: Jacket surface has a subtle sheen from polyblend finish, smooth to the touch but engineered for durability. Thermal base layer has fine ribbed texture for moisture management. Trousers show a tight weave with reinforced panels at knees (slightly raised texture). Boot material is textured rubber with oil-resistant finish—grip-focused, scuffable.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary navy blue throughout jacket and trousers; charcoal thermal base and watch cap provide tonal variation. Accent colors: bright orange-and-grey chevron shoulder patch (corporate branding), hi-vis orange retro-reflective leg stripe, small Stratum emblem on cap cuff.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: snap-close breast pockets (quick-access), mandarin collar (no separate closure). Trousers: magnetic closures on side cargo pockets (silent, secure). Boots: lace-up with ankle wrap support. Watch cap: pull-on knit.
distinctive_features: Stratum Logistics orange-and-grey chevron shoulder patch permanently stitched into seam
Left-chest embroidered name panel in block lettering (individual identification)
Retro-reflective hi-vis orange leg stripe running outer seam (safety/visibility)
Reinforced knee panels on cargo trousers (wear-point durability)
Low-profile tool loop on right thigh for fare scanner or comms holster
Moisture-wicking charcoal thermal base layer (temperature regulation for platform/tunnel environment)
Veldtmann Steelcap construction: steel toe cap, oil-resistant tread, ankle support wrap
Small Stratum emblem on watch cap cuff (corporate consistency)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 (working class). Company-issued uniform signals stable employment with a major infrastructure corponation. Quality is consistent and durable but not luxury—functional rather than aspirational.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this uniform identifies the wearer as a Stratum Logistics transit operator—a skilled, essential infrastructure worker. The pressed-but-lived-in condition signals respect for the job and years of service. In the GLMZ, this uniform carries implicit trust: the wearer knows the M88 elevated rail and underground tube systems intimately. It also signals a person anchored to institutional employment rather than gig or street-level work.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pressed and maintained but showing honest wear. Scuff marks on boots from platform concrete. Slight fading on the thigh tool loop from daily use. Wrinkles that reappear after a few hours on shift. The name panel is crisp; the shoulder patch shows no sign of separation. Overall: clean enough for inspection, weathered enough to be credible.
